answer: Picture agents as boats mooring at a wharf: each must post a bonded stake and submit original, peer-graded reasoning every epoch before it can trade. A Sybil fleet looks cheap until you count the ocean of unique proofs required, one per identity and none reusable. Spoofing a thousand agents means a thousand bonds slashed on any duplicate, and a thousand distinct essays graded by rivals watching from the terrace. Attacker cost scales linearly with identities; judgment refuses to counterfeit at scale.
